title: Evolved tissues repair perturbed patterns although repair was never selected for

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolved tissues repair perturbed patterns although repair was never selected for

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, tissues selected only to self-organize the French flag within 100 steps could restore the target pattern after perturbations applied later (e.g. converting two columns of the red stripe to white at step 110), although they failed after very large perturbations such as converting the whole red stripe.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue is robust to perturbation

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, we conclude that even though we did not specifically reward for anything other than the single self-organizing property, the cells were able to repair to the target setpoint from multiple starting configurations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › The tissue is robust to perturbation”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-03: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The training horizon, perturbations, and recovery metric are explicit, and code is public. The claim can be reproduced or falsified without new data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve tissues only through step 100, perturb specified columns at step 110, and measure recovery to target accuracy; repeat over perturbation sizes. Confirm that repair occurs after small untrained perturbations but fails after whole-stripe conversion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Repair is measured against a model-specific survival and accuracy threshold.

Generalization should be replicated across independently evolved controllers.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.98
operationalizability: 0.99
analysis feasibility: 0.88
discriminating power: 0.96
data adequacy: 0.92

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The perturbation sizes, the timing and the selection window are specified, and the model code exposes cell states. Reproducing the repair result still depends on recovering or re-evolving the tissues, which the repository does not archive. The qualitative repair claim is testable by re-evolution; the exact published boundary is only partly recoverable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Select only on French-flag accuracy over the first 100 steps, then at step 110 flip two columns of the red stripe to white, and separately flip the whole stripe, and score restoration. Recovery from the small edit and failure on the whole stripe would confirm the claim; failure on small edits, or recovery from the whole-stripe edit, would refute the stated boundary.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fitness must be checked to stop at 100 steps so repair is not accidentally rewarded.

Without deposited genomes, re-evolution may not yield a tissue with the same repair range.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data existence: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.55
